senses.gloss: (b. h.; חלל) [outside of the sanctuary, foreign,] profane, common, opp. קוֹדֶשׁ; week-day, opp. שַׁבָּת, מוֹעֵד.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 104a">Pes. 104ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 26b:12">Ḥull. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>בין קודש לח׳</he> between what is sacred and what is secular.

Shebu. 35ᵇ כל שמות … חוץ מזה שהוא ח׳ all names of lordship (Adonay) … are sacred, except the following which is secular (referring to persons).—חוֹלוֹ של מועד, or חול המועד the half-festive days intervening between the first and the last days of Passover or of Succoth.

<cite ref="Mishnah Maaser Sheni 3:8">Maas. Sh. III, 8</cite> <he>פתוחות לח׳</he> having an entrance on secular ground; <cite ref="Mishnah Maaser Sheni 3:8">ib.</cite> <he>תוכן ח׳</he> their inside is secular ground.

B. Mets. 84ᵇ כלי … ישתמש בו ח׳ shall the vessel once used for sacred things, be used for secular purposes (shall R. Eleazar’s widow marry Rabbi)?; a. v. fr.—Pl. חוּלִּין profane things, animals &c. not consecrated, ordinary objects.
<cite ref="Chullin 2b:6">Ḥull. 2ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>ח׳ שנעשו על וכ׳</he> ordinary food (not T’rumah) prepared with the precautions required for the levitical cleanness of consecrated food.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 22a:2">Pes. 22ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ח׳ שנשחטו בעזרה</he> animals not consecrated for sacrifices which were slaughtered in the Temple court.
<cite ref="Pesachim 22a:2">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>ח׳ … דאורייתא</he> the law forbidding the use of ordinary animals slaughtered &c., is not Biblical.
<cite ref="Gittin 62a:3">Gitt. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>עיסת חוּלָּיו</he> his ordinary dough; <he>זיתי חוליו</he> (not <he>ים …</he>), v. <cite ref="I00105"><he>טָהֳרָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chagigah 1:3">Ḥag. I, 3</cite> <he>באות מן הח׳</he> are procured from secular funds, opp. to proceeds from second tithes; a. fr.—

Ber. 32ᵃ (play on ויחל, Ex. XXXII, 11) ח׳ הוא לך וכ׳ it is too foreign to thy nature to do such a thing; Yalk. Gen. 83, v. חָלִילָה.—Ḥullin (= שְׁחִיטַת ח׳), name of a treatise of the Mishnah, Tosefta and Talmud Babli, of the Order of Kodashim, containing the laws concerning ordinary meat.
